claims: Sub-agent handoffs 'got way better' after adding this framework at the tail end of handoff logic from a sub-agent to the orchestrator to the next sub-agent
3,510 people on the GitHub repo waitlist; at 5,000 he shifts focus to getting the Trillion repo ready
Sharing file locations instead of file contents keeps orchestrator context from bloating
A confidence threshold lets the orchestrator send work back instead of passing it on
how_to_steps: When a sub-agent finishes, have it return a short 'sticky note' with five fields:
W — Why this is ready to move on (e.g. 'The design is finished and ready to be turned into real code')
W — What to do next (e.g. 'Build the pricing page into the actual app')
W — Where the stuff is: list of file locations edited/added, not the file contents
H — Heads up for the next sub-agent (e.g. 'The project needs React Bits installed')
H — How sure am I (percentage, e.g. 92%); orchestrator enforces a threshold and bounces work back below it
on_screen_only: Waitlist dashboard: 'LIVE COUNT 3,510 signed up so far — 1,490 to go until focused work on a deploy-ready Trillion'; progress bar 2.5K -> 5K; header mentions open-source repo drops on GitHub at 10,000

WWWHH card with the filled example: WHY: 'The design is finished and ready to be turned into real code.' WHAT TO DO: 'Build the pricing page into the actual app.' WHERE THE STUFF IS: 'A list of the file locations. Not the actual files but where they are.' HEADS UP: 'The project needs ReactBit installed.' HOW SURE AM I: '92%.'

relevance.why: Directly transferable to Claude Code subagent definitions: a fixed handoff schema with file paths and a confidence score is a practical fix for context bloat and half-finished handoffs.

implement_score.why: Add a 'final report must contain Why / What next / Where (paths) / Heads up / Confidence %' instruction to subagent prompts and have the orchestrator gate on confidence. Fifteen minutes, no tooling.

verify: Trillion is not public yet (waitlist); nothing to install
